title: Make Every Slide Earn Its Place

ciFast.note: Fast verification reruns release, format, lint, unit, proof-smoke, evaluation, build, and bundle gates after push.

ciDeep.note: Deep proof reruns build, pipeline, Chromium, Firestore rules, bundle, and strict app proof after push.

deploy.note: Deployment remains downstream of the repository's successful main workflow.

liveProvider.note: Six real public Scion browser courses pass first attempt at full scope with 29 total provider calls, zero retries, A grades, zero P0/P1/P2 findings, 38/38 export checks per package, and the adapter inactive.

manualHuman.note: Codex is the declared judge. No instructor, classroom, human-preference, accessibility-certification, or universal factual-validity claim is made.

manualBrowser.note: A resumed 99/A, Texture 97 project answers a fresh grounded Agent question, downloads a valid 631,819-byte ZIP, and remains readable at desktop and 390x844 in light and dark themes with no warning/error console entries.

claims.summary: The settlement freezes the source commit, six-course panel, tracked weights, compiler size, npm scripts, release contracts, large binaries, and bundle ceilings before the intervention.
Texture metric 1.2.0 measures learner-visible units and comparable windows while remaining diagnostic beside the frozen score.
One deterministic compiler intervention varies slide agendas, fact-ledger leads, discussion decisions, and visible labels without adding provider calls or facts.
The matched panel lowers target slide skeleton repetition from 22.22% to 17.57% on the same 29 provider calls and zero retries, with all six courses improving.
Two isolated complete-package AI judges prefer the candidate in all twelve course-order verdicts with no candidate factual or source-boundary regression.
All six candidate courses pass first attempt at full scope with complete kernels and materials, A grades, zero findings or readiness failures, and passing exports.
Rendered inspection of 221 PPTX slides and 30 DOCX pages closes four real slide-layout collisions through deterministic exporter fitting.
The current production build proves a grounded Scion Agent answer, physical valid ZIP, desktop and phone layouts, both themes, one ZIP owner, and a clean console.
The release makes no latency claim, records the slower instrumented candidate round, and keeps compiler, bundles, weights, scripts, contracts, and large binaries within unchanged ratchets.
Gemma weights remain unchanged and the adapter remains inactive; compatible providers inherit the compiler/exporter improvement while Scion retains browser-local runtime responsibilities.
